full.title: 500 रुपये का इनाम और धरती आबा का उलगुलान | Birsa Munda Full Story

about_en: The full story of Birsa Munda, the Munda tribal leader known as Dharti Aaba, from his childhood in Ulihatu to the Ulgulan revolt and the Rs 500 reward on his head. The Shorts of this series are in the playlist "धरती आबा बिरसा मुंडा की कहानी | Birsa Munda Story".
about_hi:
बिरसा मुंडा की कहानी: जिस आदिवासी नौजवान के सिर पर अंग्रेज़ों ने पाँच सौ रुपये का इनाम रखा, वह जेल में कैसे पहुँचा?
इस पूरी डॉक्यूमेंट्री में देखिए बिरसा मुंडा का सफ़र, उलिहातु के गरीब बचपन से लेकर धरती आबा और उलगुलान तक।
जानिए ज़मीन और जंगल के हक़ की वह लड़ाई, जो आज भी याद की जाती है।
facts: Birsa Munda was born on 15 November 1875 in Ulihatu, into a poor Munda family that kept moving in search of work.
He studied at Salga under Jaipal Nag, then joined the German Mission School, converted and was renamed Birsa David. He later left the school.
From 1886 to 1890 he lived in Chaibasa. His father withdrew him from school, and the family gave up Christianity and returned to the tribal religion.
Tribal land rights were being lost to thikadars and protected-forest rules. In 1895 Birsa had a vision of a supreme God, became a preacher and was called Dharti Aaba.
He declared that Queen Victoria's rule was over and the Munda Raj had begun, and told farmers to pay no rent. He was arrested on 24 August 1895 and jailed for two years.
After his release he went underground. Around Christmas 1899 about 7000 people gathered and the Ulgulan began. Violence followed in January 1900 at Etkedih and Khunti.
The administration put a reward of Rs 500 on him. His fighters were defeated at Dombari Hill, and he was arrested at Jamkopai forest on 3 February 1900.
Birsa died in jail on 9 June 1900. In 1908 the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act barred the transfer of tribal land to non-tribals, and 15 November is now Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.
